![Linux Python dev env](cover.jpg){width="98%" fig-align="center"}

Installing Python development tools on Linux can easily pollute your system environment
if done carelessly. This guide covers how to set up an isolated, reproducible Python
development workstation on Linux using `brew`, `pipx`, and modern project tooling.

## Installing Python Runtimes

First, install the target Python interpreters via Homebrew:

```bash
brew install python@3.12 python@3.13
```

## Global CLI Tools with Pipx

Development CLI utilities (such as linters, formatters, and task runners) should be
accessible globally across all terminal sessions, but should never be installed into
your default system or global Python site-packages.

The solution is `pipx`, which installs each CLI tool into its own isolated virtual
environment while exposing its binary on your `$PATH`:

```bash
brew install pipx
pipx ensurepath
pipx install argcomplete --force
```

Add `pipx` shell completions to your `~/.zshrc`:

```bash
autoload -U compinit && compinit
eval "$(register-python-argcomplete pipx)"
```

![Pipx argcomplete setup in terminal](../../assets/images/posts/24-08-11-linux-python-dev-env/1.png){width="90%"
fig-align="center"}

## Installing Core Developer Utilities

Now install your everyday terminal development tools:

```bash
pipx install --force ruff hapless poethepoet poetry pre-commit uv pytest basedpyright
```

![Installing core utilities with pipx](../../assets/images/posts/24-08-11-linux-python-dev-env/2.png){width="90%"
fig-align="center"}

### How Pipx Manages Isolation

Inspect the generated launcher for any installed tool:

```bash
nano $(which poetry)
```

![Inspecting pipx launcher shebang in nano](../../assets/images/posts/24-08-11-linux-python-dev-env/3.png){width="90%"
fig-align="center"}

Notice the shebang (`#!`) line points to an interpreter inside
`~/.local/share/pipx/venvs/poetry/bin/python`. This launcher script sets up the
execution environment before delegating to the underlying package.

Each tool installed with `pipx` lives in a dedicated, hermetic virtual environment:

```bash
ls ~/.local/share/pipx/venvs/ -la
```

![Directory listing of pipx virtual environments](../../assets/images/posts/24-08-11-linux-python-dev-env/4.png){width="90%"
fig-align="center"}

## Initializing a Project Repository

Clone or navigate into your project repository, install the dependencies, and configure
pre-commit hooks:

```bash
# Install project dependencies
poetry install

# Install and configure git pre-commit hooks
pre-commit install --install-hooks --overwrite --allow-missing-config
pre-commit autoupdate

# Run checks across all files to verify environment integrity
pre-commit run --all-files
```

With this architecture, your global tools stay isolated, dependencies never conflict,
and each repository manages its own hermetic virtual environment.
